name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Bost seeking re-election with a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge
Challenger Julie Fortier's minimal cash and no outside spending on either side
Prediction markets price Republican hold near 97 percent
model.rationale: The 22-point Republican lean, Bost's incumbency, and his roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage leave little room for an upset, and prediction markets price the Republican hold near 97 percent even with a somewhat favorable national environment for Democrats.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Bost or a sharply stronger national Democratic environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 12th District, anchored in southern Illinois, leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Mike Bost is seeking another term. Bost has raised about $1.6 million and holds more than $845,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Julie Fortier has raised roughly $159,000 with about $34,000 available and no meaningful outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 97 percent chance of holding the seat.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the district's partisan lean is about 22 points Republican, and incumbency plus the fundraising gap add to that advantage. Even with a national environment somewhat favorable to Democrats, the expected margin remains near 19 points Republican. The race is rated Safe R, with the main caveat being the absence of polling rather than any sign of competitive risk.
